reason: The cited evidence (E1-E3) strongly supports that heterogeneous grain structures enhance ductility in low-SFE single-phase alloys via back stress hardening, but none of the passages mention the specific (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy, its SFE, or its behavior under applied-field/pressure conditions; E4 only generically states that boundaries obstruct plastic deformation. Thus, the key premise that this alloy has low SFE and that the ductility mechanism will preserve caloric performance is unsupported.
premises: Heterogeneous grain structure (nano-to-micro) can improve ductility in low-SFE alloys
Low SFE facilitates twinned nanograins and stacking faults that dynamically reinforce heterogeneity
The mechanism (back stress hardening) is applicable to single-phase alloys generally
The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has low stacking fault energy
Improved ductility from heterogeneous grains translates to improved load-bearing integrity under applied-field/pressure operation
